1	package setupui
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/tui"
10	)
11	
12	// consent.go is phase 4's gate. Distilling sessions into durable facts is the
13	// only part of setup that spends money, and until this file existed it was
14	// opt-OUT: a first run distilled unless the operator happened to know about
15	// --no-backfill.
16	//
17	// Two properties matter more than the wording:
18	//
19	//   - DEFAULT NO. Bare Enter, EOF, a closed stdin, garbage twice: all skip.
20	//     Silence is never consent to spend.
21	//   - NEVER BLOCK WITHOUT A TERMINAL. A prompt in CI is a wedged pipeline, and
22	//     a wedged pipeline is a worse outcome than any amount of unspent budget.
23	//     The no-TTY path does not read stdin AT ALL — not a byte, not a peek —
24	//     which is a stronger and far more testable claim than "it defaults".
25	
26	// Override is an explicit instruction from a flag, which suppresses the prompt.
27	type Override int
28	
29	const (
30		// OverrideNone leaves the decision to the prompt.
31		OverrideNone Override = iota
32		// OverrideYes is --yes: the only way to spend without a human.
33		OverrideYes
34		// OverrideNo is --no-backfill.
35		OverrideNo
36	)
37	
38	// ConsentRequest is everything the gate needs. It carries the TTY capability
39	// explicitly rather than sniffing a file descriptor, so every path through
40	// this function is reachable from a unit test.
41	type ConsentRequest struct {
42		// Compact uses the short setup prompt instead of the verbose phase block.
43		Compact bool
44		// Sessions is how many sessions THIS run would distill: the pending pool
45		// capped by the spend budget. The cost estimate is derived from it.
46		Sessions int
47		// Total is the whole pending pool before the budget cap. When it exceeds
48		// Sessions, the prompt says both numbers — a reader deciding whether to
49		// spend needs to know the pool is 272 even when this run covers 2.
50		Total int
51		// Agent is the agent CLI that would run. Empty means none was found.
52		Agent string
53		// Model and Effort qualify the agent, for the informed-decision line.
54		Model  string
55		Effort string
56		// Override is the flag, if one was passed.
57		Override Override
58		// TTY reports whether a human can answer.
59		TTY bool
60		// ResumeCommand is the one command that starts a distill later. It is
61		// printed on every skip, because a skip that does not say how to change
62		// its mind is a dead end.
63		ResumeCommand string
64	}
65	
66	// ConsentReason is WHY consent landed where it did, as a value.
67	//
68	// Reason below is a sentence for a human. Anything that needs to branch on the
69	// outcome must branch on this instead: the short form has to tell "no agent on
70	// PATH" apart from "the human said no", and deriving that by matching English
71	// against Reason breaks the moment the sentence is reworded.
72	type ConsentReason int
73	
74	const (
75		// ConsentReasonUnset is the zero value; treat it as "not decided here".
76		ConsentReasonUnset ConsentReason = iota
77		// ConsentReasonNoBackfill is --no-backfill.
78		ConsentReasonNoBackfill
79		// ConsentReasonNoSessions is a repo with nothing recorded yet.
80		ConsentReasonNoSessions
81		// ConsentReasonNoAgent is sessions present and no CLI able to read them.
82		ConsentReasonNoAgent
83		// ConsentReasonFlagYes is --yes.
84		ConsentReasonFlagYes
85		// ConsentReasonNoTTY is a non-interactive stdin, where silence is not
86		// consent.
87		ConsentReasonNoTTY
88		// ConsentReasonAccepted is a human who answered yes.
89		ConsentReasonAccepted
90		// ConsentReasonDeclined is a human who answered no.
91		ConsentReasonDeclined
92	
93		// The four below are reached BEFORE consent is asked, so they are not
94		// consent decisions at all -- they are the reasons the question never
95		// came up. They live in this enum because the short form needs one typed
96		// answer to "why was nothing distilled", and inventing a second enum for
97		// half of it would just move the matching problem.
98	
99		// ConsentReasonPaused is `brain stop`: background work is paused, and
100		// re-running setup will skip again. The remedy is `start`.
101		ConsentReasonPaused
102		// ConsentReasonAlreadyDistilled is a re-run with nothing pending.
103		ConsentReasonAlreadyDistilled
104		// ConsentReasonAlreadyRunning is a backfill already in flight. Reporting
105		// this as "skipped" contradicts the machine's actual state.
106		ConsentReasonAlreadyRunning
107		// ConsentReasonNoExecutable is an unresolvable path to this binary, so
108		// nothing could be spawned.
109		ConsentReasonNoExecutable
110	)
111	
112	// ConsentOutcome is the decision and why it was reached.
113	type ConsentOutcome struct {
114		// Spend is the answer.
115		Spend bool
116		// Reason is always set, including when Spend is true. It is what the
117		// settled phase line says.
118		Reason string
119		// Why is the same decision as a value, for callers that must branch.
120		Why ConsentReason
121		// Prompted reports whether a human was actually asked. A test asserting
122		// "CI does not block" asserts on this, not on the answer.
123		Prompted bool
124	}
125	
126	// DefaultResumeCommand is the command printed when a distill is skipped.
127	const DefaultResumeCommand = "entire brain distill"
128	
129	// Consent decides whether phase 4 may spend.
130	//
131	// Order is load bearing. The three "spending is impossible" checks come first,
132	// so --yes in a repo with no sessions and no agent reports the truth instead of
133	// claiming it spent. Then the flags, then the terminal. The reader `in` is
134	// touched on exactly one path: a real prompt on a real terminal.
135	func Consent(req ConsentRequest, in io.Reader, out io.Writer, r *Renderer) ConsentOutcome {
136		resume := req.ResumeCommand
137		if strings.TrimSpace(resume) == "" {
138			resume = DefaultResumeCommand
139		}
140	
141		switch {
142		// Nothing to distill comes FIRST. The flag declines work; it cannot
143		// decline work that does not exist, and "not distilled (--no-backfill)"
144		// to someone whose repo has no captured sessions reports a decision
145		// instead of explaining the state.
146		case req.Sessions <= 0:
147			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "no sessions to distill; the brain is queryable now", Why: ConsentReasonNoSessions}
148		case req.Override == OverrideNo:
149			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled (--no-backfill); start later: " + resume, Why: ConsentReasonNoBackfill}
150		case req.Agent == "":
151			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "no agent CLI on PATH, nothing can distill; " + RemedyAgent, Why: ConsentReasonNoAgent}
152		case req.Override == OverrideYes:
153			return ConsentOutcome{Spend: true, Reason: "distilling " + plural(req.Sessions, "session") + " (--yes)", Why: ConsentReasonFlagYes}
154		case !req.TTY:
155			// Not a prompt, not a read, not a wait: one line and a default.
156			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled: no terminal to ask, and silence is not consent; run " + resume + " or pass --yes", Why: ConsentReasonNoTTY}
157		}
158	
159		blockLines := writePrompt(out, r, req)
160		answer, prompted, promptLines := askTwice(in, out, r, req.Compact)
161		erasePrompt(out, blockLines+promptLines)
162		if answer {
163			return ConsentOutcome{Spend: true, Reason: "distilling " + plural(req.Sessions, "session") + ", newest first", Why: ConsentReasonAccepted, Prompted: prompted}
164		}
165		return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled; the brain is queryable now, start later: " + resume, Why: ConsentReasonDeclined, Prompted: prompted}
166	}
167	
168	// writePrompt paints the block the operator is answering. It uses the same
169	// gutter as every phase line, with the glyph column left blank: a question is
170	// not an outcome and must not wear an outcome's tick.
171	func writePrompt(out io.Writer, r *Renderer, req ConsentRequest) int {
172		if out == nil {
173			return 0
174		}
175		bullet := " " + r.Bullet() + " "
176		agent := "Agent: " + req.Agent
177		if req.Model != "" {
178			agent += bullet + "model: " + req.Model
179		}
180		if req.Effort != "" {
181			agent += bullet + "effort: " + req.Effort
182		}
183		if req.Compact {
184			pool := max(req.Total, req.Sessions)
185			verb := "remain"
186			if pool == 1 {
187				verb = "remains"
188			}
189			count := 0
190			for i, text := range []string{
191				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s. Distill up to %d now?", plural(pool, "session"), verb, req.Sessions),
192				agent + bullet + "uses agent tokens",
193			} {
194				for _, line := range r.Wrap(text) {
195					if i > 0 {
196						line = r.TUI().Paint(tui.CLIMuted, line)
197					}
198					fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", line)
199					count++
200				}
201			}
202			return count
203		}
204		pool := plural(req.Sessions, "session")
205		estimate := "Estimated: ~" + plural(req.Sessions, "agent call") + ", newest first, resumable."
206		if req.Total > req.Sessions {
207			pool = plural(req.Total, "session")
208			estimate = fmt.Sprintf("Estimated: ~%s this run (spend budget), newest first, resumable.",
209				plural(req.Sessions, "agent call"))
210		}
211		lines := []Line{
212			{Title: PhaseFacts.Title(), Text: pool + " can be distilled into durable facts.", Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
213			{Text: agent, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
214			{Text: estimate, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
215			{Blank: true},
216		}
217		for _, line := range lines {
218			fmt.Fprintln(out, r.Line(line))
219		}
220		return len(lines)
221	}
222	
223	// erasePrompt clears the consent block once it is answered. The question must
224	// be ASKED — it gates token spend — but it does not have to be KEPT: after the
225	// answer the block is history, and the final summary should be the only output
226	// left on the operator's terminal. Only the real-terminal path reaches this,
227	// so the ANSI is safe; lines counts the block plus one line per prompt attempt
228	// (the operator's Enter completed each).
229	func erasePrompt(out io.Writer, lines int) {
230		if out == nil || lines <= 0 {
231			return
232		}
233		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\x1b[%dA\x1b[J", lines)
234	}
235	
236	// question is the prompt itself. "[y/N]" is not decoration: the capital is the
237	// default, and it is the default.
238	const question = "Distill now? [y/N]"
239	
240	// askTwice reads an answer, re-asking ONCE on something unrecognisable and
241	// defaulting to No after that. Two chances is the whole budget: a loop here is
242	// a different way of blocking a pipeline.
243	func askTwice(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, r *Renderer, compact bool) (answer, prompted bool, lines int) {
244		if in == nil {
245			return false, false, 0
246		}
247		reader := bufio.NewReader(in)
248		promptLine := func(text string) string {
249			if compact {
250				return "  " + text
251			}
252			return r.Line(Line{Text: text, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()})
253		}
254		for attempt := 0; attempt < 2; attempt++ {
255			// Printed with a trailing space Line would have trimmed: the cursor has to
256			// sit clear of the "]" or the answer reads as part of the question.
257			fmt.Fprint(out, promptLine(question)+" ")
258			// The operator's Enter (or the explicit newline on EOF) completes the
259			// prompt line, so each attempt occupies exactly one line for the erase.
260			lines++
261			line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
262			got := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
263			if err != nil && got == "" {
264				// EOF, a closed stdin, an interrupt that shut the pipe: No, with a
265				// newline so the next line does not land beside the prompt.
266				fmt.Fprintln(out)
267				return false, true, lines
268			}
269			switch got {
270			case "y", "yes":
271				return true, true, lines
272			case "", "n", "no":
273				return false, true, lines
274			}
275			if attempt == 0 {
276				fmt.Fprintln(out, promptLine("Please answer y or n."))
277				lines++
278			}
279			if err != nil {
280				fmt.Fprintln(out)
281				return false, true, lines
282			}
283		}

169	// gutter as every phase line, with the glyph column left blank: a question is
170	// not an outcome and must not wear an outcome's tick.
171	func writePrompt(out io.Writer, r *Renderer, req ConsentRequest) int {
172		if out == nil {
173			return 0
174		}
175		bullet := " " + r.Bullet() + " "
176		agent := "Agent: " + req.Agent

179		}

182		}

185			verb := "remain"
186			if pool == 1 {

188			}
189			count := 0
190			for i, text := range []string{

193			} {

195					if i > 0 {

197					}

199					count++
200				}
201			}
202			return count
203		}

205		estimate := "Estimated: ~" + plural(req.Sessions, "agent call") + ", newest first, resumable."
206		if req.Total > req.Sessions {
207			pool = plural(req.Total, "session")
208			estimate = fmt.Sprintf("Estimated: ~%s this run (spend budget), newest first, resumable.",
209				plural(req.Sessions, "agent call"))
210		}
211		lines := []Line{
212			{Title: PhaseFacts.Title(), Text: pool + " can be distilled into durable facts.", Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
213			{Text: agent, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
214			{Text: estimate, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
215			{Blank: true},
216		}
217		for _, line := range lines {
218			fmt.Fprintln(out, r.Line(line))
219		}
220		return len(lines)
221	}

223	// erasePrompt clears the consent block once it is answered. The question must
224	// be ASKED — it gates token spend — but it does not have to be KEPT: after the
225	// answer the block is history, and the final summary should be the only output
226	// left on the operator's terminal. Only the real-terminal path reaches this,
227	// so the ANSI is safe; lines counts the block plus one line per prompt attempt
228	// (the operator's Enter completed each).
229	func erasePrompt(out io.Writer, lines int) {
230		if out == nil || lines <= 0 {
231			return
232		}
233		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\x1b[%dA\x1b[J", lines)
234	}
235	
236	// question is the prompt itself. "[y/N]" is not decoration: the capital is the
237	// default, and it is the default.
238	const question = "Distill now? [y/N]"
239	
240	// askTwice reads an answer, re-asking ONCE on something unrecognisable and
241	// defaulting to No after that. Two chances is the whole budget: a loop here is
242	// a different way of blocking a pipeline.
243	func askTwice(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, r *Renderer, compact bool) (answer, prompted bool, lines int) {
244		if in == nil {
245			return false, false, 0
246		}
247		reader := bufio.NewReader(in)
248		promptLine := func(text string) string {
249			if compact {
250				return "  " + text
251			}
252			return r.Line(Line{Text: text, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()})
253		}
254		for attempt := 0; attempt < 2; attempt++ {
255			// Printed with a trailing space Line would have trimmed: the cursor has to
256			// sit clear of the "]" or the answer reads as part of the question.
257			fmt.Fprint(out, promptLine(question)+" ")
258			// The operator's Enter (or the explicit newline on EOF) completes the
259			// prompt line, so each attempt occupies exactly one line for the erase.
260			lines++
261			line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
262			got := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
263			if err != nil && got == "" {
264				// EOF, a closed stdin, an interrupt that shut the pipe: No, with a
265				// newline so the next line does not land beside the prompt.
266				fmt.Fprintln(out)
267				return false, true, lines
268			}
269			switch got {
270			case "y", "yes":
271				return true, true, lines
272			case "", "n", "no":
273				return false, true, lines
274			}
275			if attempt == 0 {
276				fmt.Fprintln(out, promptLine("Please answer y or n."))
277				lines++
278			}
279			if err != nil {
280				fmt.Fprintln(out)
281				return false, true, lines
282			}
283		}
284		return false, true, lines
285	}

The naming mismatch looks minor, and I'm noting where the hosted/local prompt is supposed to appear in the sequence.

The doc says to get a token via `entire auth token`, but connect.go only records a non-secret binding, and the token is minted during each sync, so the doc's sequence is roughly right. The real issue is error handling: runConnect writes the binding before the first pull runs, so if that pull fails, a binding is already on disk. That conflicts with the requirement that a failure leave no binding behind, so reusing runConnect unchanged won't work.

I'm now checking whether setup calls runConnect directly or rebuilds the steps from the connect.Deps pieces, since the binding is written before the first sync. I also need to see if the sync engine reads the binding from disk, because that decides whether failure cleanup means deleting a written binding or passing it in memory.

I'm going to check the feed cache to see whether raw feed items keep their session IDs, and whether the session manifest and the daemon's periodic distill trigger line up with the shared-check idea.

I verified the document against the code (setup phases, `connect.Deps`, `hostedFactsSyncAndPull`, the feed cache, fact anchors, the distill cache, `setupui`, `internal/tui`). Brain preflight ran and the brief surfaced the COR-2128/COR-2229 decisions; the brief's own warning says the graph search store is not built for this commit, so I verified structure by direct source reads. The document's mechanical claims all check out (bubbletea/bubbles are real dependencies, `tui.DetectCaps` exists, provenance anchors carry `SessionID`/`CheckpointID`, the daemon's distill goes through `runDistill` so a shared coverage check is feasible, the stale COR-2029 text is at `internal/setupui/detect.go:177`).

Four questions remain where a wrong guess would matter, ranked:

**1. Does the covered-session set suppress re-distillation of sessions whose content changed?**
The covered set includes the local `facts.ndjson` provenance, so any session that ever yielded one fact is "covered" forever — including on the machine that distilled it. Today the distill cache (`internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:588-636`) re-dispatches a session when its fingerprint or chunk hashes change (sessions grow). Step 5 applies the covered-set check to the daemon's periodic runs too. If the check applies to all facts, grown sessions silently stop producing new facts (a regression); if it applies only to sessions absent from the local distill cache, or only to remotely-pulled facts, the incremental path survives. The formula "manifest minus covered minus cache hits" does not settle this. The answer decides where the check sits in `runDistill`'s session selection and what the daemon does.

**2. What happens to the binding when the first sync fails?**
The anti-goal says any hosted failure leaves setup local-only "without writing a binding." But `HostedFactsSyncAndPull` reads the binding from disk (`internal/cli/hosted_sync.go:84`), so the binding must be written before the sync can run, and connect's current contract on a failed first pull is "stays bound, re-run connect" (`connect.go:164-171`). The options differ structurally: roll back `hosted.json` (and the just-installed pre-push hook, and any `NoAccessUntil` write), plumb an in-memory binding through a changed sync signature, or read "without writing a binding" as covering only pre-bind failures (no host CLI, not logged in, placement denied). Each produces a different refactor of connect and a different setup re-run behavior.

**3. How does setup treat an opted-out (disconnected) repo?**
`entire brain disconnect` keeps `hosted.json` with `OptedOut: true`, and `setup.json` may remember "hosted" from before the disconnect. Skip rules 1–2 as written ("a hosted binding already exists → hosted"; "remembered choice → that choice") would silently re-bind and re-sync a repo the user explicitly disconnected. That contradicts a recorded invariant: "a bare setup after a disconnect must not resurrect the hook" (`internal/cli/setup.go:2489-2491`). Intended behavior — treat opted-out as local, re-prompt, or let the remembered choice win — changes both skip-rule logic and whether disconnect must also clear the setup record.

**4. Can `--local-only` override an existing binding?**
The skip rules are ordered, and the binding check comes before the flags, so a user who passes `--local-only` on a bound repo still gets the hosted path and a network sync. Is the flag ignored, an error, or respected for this run without unbinding? This decides the flag's validation logic and matters because it is the user's only no-network lever during setup besides `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS`.

One smaller gap, flaggable in the plan rather than blocking: when the hosted path fails and setup continues local-only, is "hosted" still recorded in `setup.json`? Recorded → every re-run silently retries the network path; not recorded → every re-run re-prompts. The document is silent on which.
